sources.text:
QA Process Handbook
Section: 4 Flaky test policy

### 4 Flaky test policy

A test is **flaky** when it fails and then passes on retry within the same build. TestNG reports the failed attempt as SKIPPED, so watch the skip count.

- Two flaky builds within 7 days: quarantine the test with the Jira label `flaky` and fix it within the sprint.
- `RetryAnalyzer` keeps `maxRetryCount = 3`. Never raise it to hide a failure.
- Playwright uses `retries: 2` on CI only. A test that fails all retries is a real failure, not a flake.
- Common root causes: hard sleeps (`Thread.sleep`, `waitJVM`, `page.waitForTimeout`), shared test users across parallel workers, and order-dependent data.

Section: Introduction

CI Test Pipeline (Lucid chart exported to text) Owner: Rahul Verma (DevOps)   Last edited: 2026-04-12

Jenkins jobs

- vwo-selenium-regression: nightly at 02:00 IST (Started by timer) and on demand
- playwright-e2e: on every push to main of AdvancePlaywrightFramework1x

Flow: vwo-selenium-regression Checkout -> Build (mvn compile) -> Login health check (proposed) -> Selenium Regression (mvn test with a TestNG suite XML) -> Publish Allure -> Notify Slack #qa-alerts

Flow: playwright-e2e Install (npm ci, playwright install chromium) -> Playwright E2E (CI=true, 4 workers, retries 2) -> Publish Report (HTML + results.json) -> Notify Slack #qa-alerts

Agents

- Egress: Cloud NAT 35.200.14.7 (must be on the VWO test account IP allowlist)
- Previous on-prem agents egressed via 203.0.113.24 (decommissioned 2026-04-03)

Result handling

- FAILURE: Slack alert with failed test names and the Allure link
- UNSTABLE: Playwright tests failed after retries; triage in the daily standup
- Retried-then-passed tests are flaky; two flaky builds in 7 days puts the test in quarantine

Section: 4 How we work

## 4 How we work

Every bug links a test case ID and, for CI failures, a Jenkins build number. Before filing a bug, search Jira and ask QABuddy for duplicates. A login failure with valid credentials is treated as S1 until it is proven to be environment-specific.

When a test fails on CI but passes locally, check the environment first: IP allowlists, expired test accounts and shared users in parallel runs caused most of the CI failures this quarter.

sources.text:
QA Process Handbook
Section: 3 Bug triage > 3.1 Severity vs priority, 3.2 Triage rules

#### 3.1 Severity vs priority

Severity is the technical impact; priority is how soon we fix it. Triage sets both.

| Severity | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | System or security failure, no workaround | Users cannot log in with valid credentials |
| S2 | Major feature broken, workaround exists | A/B test report does not load |
| S3 | Minor feature or UI issue | Misaligned button on the support page |
| S4 | Cosmetic | Typo in a tooltip |

#### 3.2 Triage rules

1. Search Jira and QABuddy for duplicates before filing. Mark duplicates and link the original (VWO-33 is a duplicate of VWO-26).
2. Every bug links the failing test case ID and, for CI failures, the Jenkins build number.
3. A login failure for valid credentials is S1 until proven to be environment-specific.
4. Environment issues (IP allowlists, expired test accounts, agent problems) are filed in the QAB project, not as product bugs.

Meeting: 2026-04-07 Login Failure Triage Meeting (2026-04-07)
Meeting: Login failure triage (VWO-26, VWO-33, CI build #142)
Date: 2026-04-07
Attendees: Pramod (QA Lead), Ananya Rao (SDET), Rahul Verma (DevOps), Meera Iyer (Product Manager)

[00:00:12] Pramod: Thanks for joining. We have two user reports, VWO-26 and VWO-33, both say login fails with valid credentials. And since Sunday our nightly vwo-selenium-regression job, build 142, fails every positive login test.
[00:00:41] Ananya: On CI the failure is a TimeoutException in WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement, waiting for the dashboard user name, xpath //h6. The screenshot listener captured the banner though: "Your email, password, IP address or location did not match". So the dashboard wait is a symptom. Login itself is being rejected.
[00:01:20] Meera: Is this a product bug? Customers saw it too.
[00:01:34] Ananya: I don't think it is one bug. Locally the same credentials work. It only fails from the new GCP agents.
[00:01:52] Rahul: That lines up. We moved the Jenkins agents to GCP last Friday. The old on-prem agents went out through 203.0.113.24. The new pool uses a Cloud NAT, 35.200.14.7. If the VWO test account has an IP allowlist, the new IP is not on it.
[00:02:30] Pramod: And the error text literally says IP address or location. So for CI the root cause is the egress IP change, not the framework.
[00:02:48] Meera: What about the customer tickets?
[00:03:05] Pramod: VWO-33 is the same symptom as VWO-26, so I will mark 33 as a duplicate. For customers, product should check whether the location check fires for users behind corporate VPNs. That is a separate investigation, owner Meera.
[00:03:40] Ananya: One more thing. Even once login works, LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds uses waitJVM 5000, a Thread.sleep. That will make the positive test flaky on slow days. We should replace it with an explicit wait.
[00:04:02] Pramod: Agreed, but separately. Do not bump the RetryAnalyzer max retry count to hide it. It is already 3.

Meeting: Login failure triage (VWO-26, VWO-33, CI build #142)
Date: 2026-04-07
Attendees: Pramod (QA Lead), Ananya Rao (SDET), Rahul Verma (DevOps), Meera Iyer (Product Manager)

[00:00:12] Pramod: Thanks for joining. We have two user reports, VWO-26 and VWO-33, both say login fails with valid credentials. And since Sunday our nightly vwo-selenium-regression job, build 142, fails every positive login test.
[00:00:41] Ananya: On CI the failure is a TimeoutException in WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement, waiting for the dashboard user name, xpath //h6. The screenshot listener captured the banner though: "Your email, password, IP address or location did not match". So the dashboard wait is a symptom. Login itself is being rejected.
[00:01:20] Meera: Is this a product bug? Customers saw it too.
[00:01:34] Ananya: I don't think it is one bug. Locally the same credentials work. It only fails from the new GCP agents.
[00:01:52] Rahul: That lines up. We moved the Jenkins agents to GCP last Friday. The old on-prem agents went out through 203.0.113.24. The new pool uses a Cloud NAT, 35.200.14.7. If the VWO test account has an IP allowlist, the new IP is not on it.
[00:02:30] Pramod: And the error text literally says IP address or location. So for CI the root cause is the egress IP change, not the framework.
[00:02:48] Meera: What about the customer tickets?
[00:03:05] Pramod: VWO-33 is the same symptom as VWO-26, so I will mark 33 as a duplicate. For customers, product should check whether the location check fires for users behind corporate VPNs. That is a separate investigation, owner Meera.
[00:03:40] Ananya: One more thing. Even once login works, LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds uses waitJVM 5000, a Thread.sleep. That will make the positive test flaky on slow days. We should replace it with an explicit wait.
[00:04:02] Pramod: Agreed, but separately. Do not bump the RetryAnalyzer max retry count to hide it. It is already 3.

QA Process Handbook
Section: 3 Bug triage > 3.1 Severity vs priority, 3.2 Triage rules

#### 3.1 Severity vs priority

Severity is the technical impact; priority is how soon we fix it. Triage sets both.

| Severity | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | System or security failure, no workaround | Users cannot log in with valid credentials |
| S2 | Major feature broken, workaround exists | A/B test report does not load |
| S3 | Minor feature or UI issue | Misaligned button on the support page |
| S4 | Cosmetic | Typo in a tooltip |

#### 3.2 Triage rules

1. Search Jira and QABuddy for duplicates before filing. Mark duplicates and link the original (VWO-33 is a duplicate of VWO-26).
2. Every bug links the failing test case ID and, for CI failures, the Jenkins build number.
3. A login failure for valid credentials is S1 until proven to be environment-specific.
4. Environment issues (IP allowlists, expired test accounts, agent problems) are filed in the QAB project, not as product bugs.

QA Onboarding Guide
Section: 3 Running the tests locally > 3.1 Selenium, 3.2 Playwright

### 3.1 Selenium

Install Java 17 and Maven. From the repository root run mvn test - Dsurefire.suiteXmlFiles=testng_vwo_prop_improved_pom_part3.xml. Configuration such as the VWO URL and test accounts comes from src/main/resources/data.properties.

### 3.2 Playwright

Install Node 20, run npm ci and npx playwright install chromium, then npx playwright test. Set TTA_ENV to qa, stage or prod to switch the base URL. Locally there are no retries; on CI there are two.

Meeting: 2026-04-07 Login Failure Triage Meeting (2026-04-07)
Meeting: Login failure triage (VWO-26, VWO-33, CI build #142)
Date: 2026-04-07
Attendees: Pramod (QA Lead), Ananya Rao (SDET), Rahul Verma (DevOps), Meera Iyer (Product Manager)

[00:00:12] Pramod: Thanks for joining. We have two user reports, VWO-26 and VWO-33, both say login fails with valid credentials. And since Sunday our nightly vwo-selenium-regression job, build 142, fails every positive login test.
[00:00:41] Ananya: On CI the failure is a TimeoutException in WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement, waiting for the dashboard user name, xpath //h6. The screenshot listener captured the banner though: "Your email, password, IP address or location did not match". So the dashboard wait is a symptom. Login itself is being rejected.
[00:01:20] Meera: Is this a product bug? Customers saw it too.
[00:01:34] Ananya: I don't think it is one bug. Locally the same credentials work. It only fails from the new GCP agents.
[00:01:52] Rahul: That lines up. We moved the Jenkins agents to GCP last Friday. The old on-prem agents went out through 203.0.113.24. The new pool uses a Cloud NAT, 35.200.14.7. If the VWO test account has an IP allowlist, the new IP is not on it.
[00:02:30] Pramod: And the error text literally says IP address or location. So for CI the root cause is the egress IP change, not the framework.
[00:02:48] Meera: What about the customer tickets?
[00:03:05] Pramod: VWO-33 is the same symptom as VWO-26, so I will mark 33 as a duplicate. For customers, product should check whether the location check fires for users behind corporate VPNs. That is a separate investigation, owner Meera.
[00:03:40] Ananya: One more thing. Even once login works, LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds uses waitJVM 5000, a Thread.sleep. That will make the positive test flaky on slow days. We should replace it with an explicit wait.
[00:04:02] Pramod: Agreed, but separately. Do not bump the RetryAnalyzer max retry count to hide it. It is already 3.

**Symptom**  
- Build **vwo‑selenium‑regression #142** fails in the Selenium Regression stage.  
- Positive login tests `TestVWOLogin_01_Normal_POM.testLoginPositiveVWO` and `TestVWOLogin_03_Prop_Improved_POM.testLoginPositiveVWO` throw `TimeoutException` waiting for the dashboard user name element `//h6` (20 s) and the screenshot shows the banner **“Your email, password, IP address or location did not match”**[3][4].  

**Root cause**  
- The new Jenkins agent pool (GCP) egresses through IP **35.200.14.7**, which is **not on the VWO test account allowlist**. VWO blocks the login, returning the “IP address or location did not match” message, so the dashboard element never appears, causing the timeout. This is an **environment problem** (IP allowlist mismatch), not a product bug or test‑framework issue[2][5].  

**Flaky or real?**  
- The failure is **real**; it occurs consistently on every CI run after the agent migration. Retries are not recommended (action item explicitly says *do not increase RetryAnalyzer maxRetryCount to mask failures*)[2][5].  

**Related tickets**  
- **QAB‑101** – CI login tests fail after Jenkins agent migration (the ticket being fixed)[1].  
- **VWO‑26** – Customer reports of login failure (investigated separately)[5].  
- **VWO‑33** – Duplicate of VWO‑26 (marked duplicate)[2][5].  

**Fix and next steps**  
1. **Add the new egress IP to the VWO allowlist** – Rahul Verma to add **35.200.14.7** (due 2026‑04‑08)[2].  
2. **Add a “login health check” pre‑flight stage** to the regression suite to detect allowlist issues early (due 2026‑04‑15)[2].  
3. **Replace `WaitHelpers.waitJVM(5000)` with an explicit wait** in `LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds` to reduce flakiness once login works (due 2026‑04‑12)[2].  
4. **Do not increase RetryAnalyzer** – keep maxRetryCount at 3 to avoid masking the real issue[5].  

After the IP is whitelisted, the login will succeed, the dashboard `<h6>` element will become visible, and the Selenium regression build should pass.

**Symptom**  
- `testLoginPositiveVWO` fails on the first attempt (TimeoutException waiting for `//h6`) and passes on retry 1. In build #143 it is counted as *skipped* (failed attempt) while the build is green[5]. In build #142 it fails outright (no retry) with the same timeout[7].  

**Root cause**  
- The test uses a hard `Thread.sleep(5000)` in `LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds()` instead of waiting for the dashboard element. When the dashboard loads slower than 5 s + 20 s explicit wait, the first attempt times out[2].  
- This is a **product‑test framework bug** (wait implementation), not an environment issue (the NAT IP allowlist fix already applied in build #143)[1].  

**Flaky or real?**  
- Flaky: the test passes on retry 1 in build #143, indicating nondeterministic timing rather than a consistent failure[5]. The retry analyzer masks the failure as a *skipped* test, which is the early flaky signal noted in the regression health meeting[1].  

**Related tickets**  
- QAB‑102 – “Flaky: testLoginPositiveVWO passes only on retry, dashboard renders after the hard 5s sleep” (bug, in‑progress)[2].  
- QAB‑101 – NAT IP allowlist fix that made build #143 green; unrelated to this flakiness[1][6].  

**Fix and next steps**  
1. Replace the `Thread.sleep(5000)` in `LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds()` with a proper explicit wait, e.g.:  
   ```java
   // LoginPage.java
   public void loginToVWOLoginValidCreds(String user, String pass) {
       // ...enter credentials...
       WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement(By.xpath("//h6")); // wait for dashboard header
   }
   ```  
   (as drafted in the PR comment by Ananya Rao)[3].  
2. Remove the test from quarantine and keep `maxRetryCount` at 0 per flaky‑test policy[4].  
3. Run a verification suite (≥20 consecutive green runs locally) to confirm stability[3].  
4. Merge the PR, trigger a new CI build, and ensure `testLoginPositiveVWO` reports 0 failures and 0 skips.

Description:
playwright-e2e build #88 failed: e2e-checkout.spec.ts "should complete checkout successfully" asserts cartPage.rowCount() toBe(1) at line 56 but receives 2. It failed on the first run and on both CI retries (retries: 2 in playwright.config.ts), so this is a real failure, not a flake.

Actual result: The cart contains an item added by another worker.

Section: 2 Test case standards > 2.1 Test case IDs, 2.2 Required fields, 2.3 Priority definitions

#### 2.1 Test case IDs

IDs follow `MODULE-NNN`, for example `LOGIN-002`, `ADMIN-014`, `SUPPORT-051`, `ABTEST-007`. The module prefix must match one of: LOGIN, VALID, INVALID, ADMIN, ADMINLOGGED, SUPPORT, ABTEST. New modules need QA Lead approval.

#### 2.2 Required fields

Every test case has: Scenario TID, TestCase Description (starting with "Verify"), PreCondition, TestSteps, Expected Result, Priority and Is Automated. Steps are numbered and separated by " | " in the CSV export.

#### 2.3 Priority definitions

- **Critical**: blocks login, payment, data security or a release. Must be automated first.
- **High**: core feature broken with no workaround.
- **Medium**: feature works with a workaround, or a cosmetic issue in a core flow.

Section: 3 Bug triage > 3.1 Severity vs priority, 3.2 Triage rules

#### 3.1 Severity vs priority

Severity is the technical impact; priority is how soon we fix it. Triage sets both.

| Severity | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | System or security failure, no workaround | Users cannot log in with valid credentials |
| S2 | Major feature broken, workaround exists | A/B test report does not load |
| S3 | Minor feature or UI issue | Misaligned button on the support page |
| S4 | Cosmetic | Typo in a tooltip |

#### 3.2 Triage rules

1. Search Jira and QABuddy for duplicates before filing. Mark duplicates and link the original (VWO-33 is a duplicate of VWO-26).
2. Every bug links the failing test case ID and, for CI failures, the Jenkins build number.
3. A login failure for valid credentials is S1 until proven to be environment-specific.
4. Environment issues (IP allowlists, expired test accounts, agent problems) are filed in the QAB project, not as product bugs.

sources.text:
Meeting: 2026-04-07 Login Failure Triage Meeting (2026-04-07)
Meeting: Login failure triage (VWO-26, VWO-33, CI build #142)
Date: 2026-04-07
Attendees: Pramod (QA Lead), Ananya Rao (SDET), Rahul Verma (DevOps), Meera Iyer (Product Manager)

[00:00:12] Pramod: Thanks for joining. We have two user reports, VWO-26 and VWO-33, both say login fails with valid credentials. And since Sunday our nightly vwo-selenium-regression job, build 142, fails every positive login test.
[00:00:41] Ananya: On CI the failure is a TimeoutException in WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement, waiting for the dashboard user name, xpath //h6. The screenshot listener captured the banner though: "Your email, password, IP address or location did not match". So the dashboard wait is a symptom. Login itself is being rejected.
[00:01:20] Meera: Is this a product bug? Customers saw it too.
[00:01:34] Ananya: I don't think it is one bug. Locally the same credentials work. It only fails from the new GCP agents.
[00:01:52] Rahul: That lines up. We moved the Jenkins agents to GCP last Friday. The old on-prem agents went out through 203.0.113.24. The new pool uses a Cloud NAT, 35.200.14.7. If the VWO test account has an IP allowlist, the new IP is not on it.
[00:02:30] Pramod: And the error text literally says IP address or location. So for CI the root cause is the egress IP change, not the framework.
[00:02:48] Meera: What about the customer tickets?
[00:03:05] Pramod: VWO-33 is the same symptom as VWO-26, so I will mark 33 as a duplicate. For customers, product should check whether the location check fires for users behind corporate VPNs. That is a separate investigation, owner Meera.
[00:03:40] Ananya: One more thing. Even once login works, LoginPage.loginToVWOLoginValidCreds uses waitJVM 5000, a Thread.sleep. That will make the positive test flaky on slow days. We should replace it with an explicit wait.
[00:04:02] Pramod: Agreed, but separately. Do not bump the RetryAnalyzer max retry count to hide it. It is already 3.

Description:

QA Process Handbook
Section: 3 Bug triage > 3.1 Severity vs priority, 3.2 Triage rules

#### 3.1 Severity vs priority

Severity is the technical impact; priority is how soon we fix it. Triage sets both.

| Severity | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | System or security failure, no workaround | Users cannot log in with valid credentials |
| S2 | Major feature broken, workaround exists | A/B test report does not load |
| S3 | Minor feature or UI issue | Misaligned button on the support page |
| S4 | Cosmetic | Typo in a tooltip |

#### 3.2 Triage rules

1. Search Jira and QABuddy for duplicates before filing. Mark duplicates and link the original (VWO-33 is a duplicate of VWO-26).
2. Every bug links the failing test case ID and, for CI failures, the Jenkins build number.
3. A login failure for valid credentials is S1 until proven to be environment-specific.
4. Environment issues (IP allowlists, expired test accounts, agent problems) are filed in the QAB project, not as product bugs.

sources.text:
Automation Coding Standards
Section: 2 Playwright framework (AdvancePlaywrightFramework1x) > 2.1 Structure, 2.2 Locators, 2.3 Waits and assertions, 2.4 API tests, 2.5 Parallel safety, 2.6 Tags

#### 2.1 Structure

- Page objects live in `src/pages`, extend `BasePage`, and are exported from `src/pages/index.ts`.
- Tests import `test` and `expect` from `@fixtures/test-base` (UI) or `@fixtures/booker.fixture` (API), never directly from `@playwright/test`.
- Wrap meaningful steps in `visualStep(page, 'title', async () => { ... })` so the report gets a screenshot per step.

#### 2.2 Locators

- Use `data-test` attributes: `page.locator('[data-test="checkout"]')`, or role-based locators such as `getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })`.
- No CSS chains that depend on layout.

#### 2.3 Waits and assertions

- Rely on web-first assertions (`await expect(locator).toContainText(...)`). Never use `page.waitForTimeout`.
- Default timeouts come from `playwright.config.ts`: test 60 s, expect 10 s.

#### 2.4 API tests

- Use `ApiHelper` or `BookingApi` instead of raw `request` calls once a test grows past one request.
- Validate responses against JSON schema with `schemaValidator` (AJV).
- Get auth tokens from the `bookerToken` fixture, not inside the test.

#### 2.5 Parallel safety

- `fullyParallel: true` with 4 workers on CI. Tests must not share mutable server-side state.
- Use a worker-scoped user per worker for anything with a cart, profile or settings (see QAB-103).

#### 2.6 Tags

Tag suites in the describe title: `@P0`, `@Regression`, `@e2e`, plus a feature tag such as `@Checkout`.

sources.text:
Jira QAB-101: CI login tests fail with "IP address or location did not match" after Jenkins agent migration
Type: Bug | Status: Done | Priority: High | Project: QABuddy Sample | Resolution: Fixed
Reporter: Ananya Rao | Assignee: Rahul Verma | Created: 05/Apr/26 | Updated: 08/Apr/26
Labels: ci, login, environment | Components: CI, Login

Description:
Since build #142 of vwo-selenium-regression, every positive login test fails on CI while passing locally.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Run testng_vwo_prop_improved_pom_part3.xml on any agent in the new GCP pool (ci-agent-gcp-01..04).
2. testLoginPositiveVWO submits valid credentials from data.properties.
3. The dashboard user name (//h6) never appears and WaitHelpers.visibilityOfElement times out after 20 s.

Expected result: Valid credentials log in and the dashboard shows the user name.
Actual result: VWO shows "Your email, password, IP address or location did not match" and stays on the login page. Screenshot attached by ScreenshotListener.

Suspected cause: VWO account security rejects logins from unrecognised IP ranges. The new agent pool egresses through a different NAT IP than the old on-prem agents.
Related: VWO-26, VWO-33 (same symptom reported by users).

## Automation Coding Standards

Sample company document generated for testing QABuddy. Applies to the Selenium (Java) and Playwright (TypeScript) frameworks.

#### 1.1 Structure

- Page classes live in `src/main/java/com/thetestingacademy/pages`. New VWO pages go in the `improved_POM` package.
- Tests live in `src/test/java/com/thetestingacademy/tests` and extend `CommonToAllTest`.
- Page classes extend `CommonToAllPage` and use its `enterInput`, `clickElement` and `getText` helpers.
- Get the driver from `DriverManager.getDriver()`. Never create a `ChromeDriver` inside a test.

#### 1.2 Locators

- Declare locators as `private By` fields at the top of the page class, for example `private By username = By.id("login-username");`.
- Prefer `By.id` and stable `data-qa` attributes over long XPaths. `By.xpath("//h6")` is too generic for new code.

#### 1.3 Waits

- Use the explicit waits in `WaitHelpers`: `visibilityOfElement`, `presenceOfElement`, `checkVisibility`.
- `WaitHelpers.waitJVM` wraps `Thread.sleep`. It is legacy: do not use it in new code, and replace it when you touch a method that calls it.
- Do not mix implicit and explicit waits.

#### 1.4 Test data and config

- Read configuration with `PropertiesReader.readKey("key")` from `data.properties`.
- Data-driven tests read Excel through `UtilExcel` with a TestNG `@DataProvider`.

#### 1.5 Retries, listeners and reporting

- Attach `RetryAnalyzer` only to suites that need it (see `testng_vwo_retry_prop_improved_pom_part4.xml`). The retry ceiling is 3.
- `ScreenshotListener` captures a screenshot on failure; keep it enabled on CI.
- Every test has Allure `@Owner` and `@Description` annotations.

Section: Element Utilities (UtilElementLocator)

### Element Utilities (UtilElementLocator)

**Concept:** `UtilElementLocator` is a thin wrapper around Playwright's `Locator` that exposes intent-revealing action helpers (`click`, `fill`, `getText`, `waitForVisible`, ...) and accepts either a CSS string **or** a built `Locator` via the `Flex` type.

**Why:** Page Objects shouldn't repeat `await page.locator(sel).click({ timeout })` everywhere. One wrapper centralises timeouts, logging, and the string-or-Locator ambiguity.

**Q&A — why use this?**

- **Q: Why the `Flex = string | Locator` type?** A: Call sites pass `'[data-test="username"]'` *or* `page.getByTestId('username')` — the wrapper normalises both via `toLocator()`.
- **Q: Where do the debug logs come from?** A: Each instance owns a scoped Winston logger (`createLogger(scope)`); actions like `click`/`fill` emit a `debug` line.
- **Q: Why keep a `type()` method when Playwright deprecated `.type()`?** A: It maps to `pressSequentially()` under the hood but keeps a name students recognise.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["target: Flex (string | Locator)"] --> B{typeof string?}
    B -->|Yes| C["page.locator(target)"]
    B -->|No| D[use Locator as-is]
    C --> E[action: click / fill / getText ...]
    D --> E
    E --> F[log.debug + Playwright call]
```

```ts
import { UtilElementLocator } from '@utils/UtilElementLocator';

const el = new UtilElementLocator(page, 'LoginPage');
await el.fill('[data-test="username"]', 'standard_user');
await el.click(page.getByTestId('login-button'));
await el.waitForVisible('[data-test="inventory-container"]');
```

---

Section: 2 Playwright framework (AdvancePlaywrightFramework1x) > 2.1 Structure, 2.2 Locators, 2.3 Waits and assertions, 2.4 API tests, 2.5 Parallel safety, 2.6 Tags

#### 2.1 Structure

- Page objects live in `src/pages`, extend `BasePage`, and are exported from `src/pages/index.ts`.
- Tests import `test` and `expect` from `@fixtures/test-base` (UI) or `@fixtures/booker.fixture` (API), never directly from `@playwright/test`.
- Wrap meaningful steps in `visualStep(page, 'title', async () => { ... })` so the report gets a screenshot per step.

#### 2.2 Locators

- Use `data-test` attributes: `page.locator('[data-test="checkout"]')`, or role-based locators such as `getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' })`.
- No CSS chains that depend on layout.

#### 2.3 Waits and assertions

- Rely on web-first assertions (`await expect(locator).toContainText(...)`). Never use `page.waitForTimeout`.
- Default timeouts come from `playwright.config.ts`: test 60 s, expect 10 s.

#### 2.4 API tests

- Use `ApiHelper` or `BookingApi` instead of raw `request` calls once a test grows past one request.
- Validate responses against JSON schema with `schemaValidator` (AJV).
- Get auth tokens from the `bookerToken` fixture, not inside the test.

#### 2.5 Parallel safety

- `fullyParallel: true` with 4 workers on CI. Tests must not share mutable server-side state.
- Use a worker-scoped user per worker for anything with a cart, profile or settings (see QAB-103).

#### 2.6 Tags

Tag suites in the describe title: `@P0`, `@Regression`, `@e2e`, plus a feature tag such as `@Checkout`.

QA Process Handbook
Section: 4 Flaky test policy

### 4 Flaky test policy

A test is **flaky** when it fails and then passes on retry within the same build. TestNG reports the failed attempt as SKIPPED, so watch the skip count.

- Two flaky builds within 7 days: quarantine the test with the Jira label `flaky` and fix it within the sprint.
- `RetryAnalyzer` keeps `maxRetryCount = 3`. Never raise it to hide a failure.
- Playwright uses `retries: 2` on CI only. A test that fails all retries is a real failure, not a flake.
- Common root causes: hard sleeps (`Thread.sleep`, `waitJVM`, `page.waitForTimeout`), shared test users across parallel workers, and order-dependent data.

- `RetryAnalyzer` implements TestNG’s `IRetryAnalyzer`.  
- It keeps an internal counter `retryCount` that starts at 0.  
- On each failed test invocation, `retry()` checks if `retryCount < maxRetryCount`. If true, it increments `retryCount` and returns **true** so TestNG will re‑run the test; otherwise it returns **false** and the test is marked failed.  
- The maximum number of retries is defined by the constant `maxRetryCount = 3`[1].  

The QA handbook reinforces that this limit must not be increased, as it is the standard flaky‑test policy[2].
